---
title: "Colour palettes"
description: >
  Every palette of bioToolkit with the index and hex code of each colour, its
  source, and the plots that use it by default.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_common.R")

# Palette cards ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Each palette is drawn in HTML (not as a figure), so that its name and hex
# codes can be searched and copied: hovering a swatch shows "index: hex".

# Escape text placed in HTML
html_escape <- function(x) {
    x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
    x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
    gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
}

# White index numbers on dark colours, black on light ones (as show_palettes())
text_colour <- function(cols) {
    rgb <- grDevices::col2rgb(cols)
    ifelse(colSums(rgb * c(0.299, 0.587, 0.114)) < 140, "#fff", "#000")
}

# One palette: its name, number of colours, swatches (or a ramp for the
# palettes defined by 256 colours) and source
palette_card <- function(name,
                         n,
                         source) {
    cols <- bt_palette(name)
    body <- if (length(cols) > 102) {
        # A smooth ramp through 16 of its colours
        stops <- bt_palette(name, 16)
        paste0(
            "<div class=\"bt-ramp\" style=\"background: linear-gradient(to right, ",
            paste(stops, collapse = ", "),
            ");\" title=\"", stops[1], " to ", stops[16], "\"></div>"
        )
    } else {
        swatches <- paste0(
            "<span class=\"bt-swatch\" style=\"background:", cols,
            "; color:", text_colour(cols), ";\" title=\"", seq_along(cols), ": ", cols, "\">",
            seq_along(cols), "</span>",
            collapse = ""
        )
        paste0("<div class=\"bt-swatches\">", swatches, "</div>")
    }
    paste0(
        "<div class=\"bt-palette\" id=\"palette-", name, "\">",
        "<div class=\"bt-palette-head\"><code>", name, "</code>",
        "<span class=\"bt-palette-n\">", n, " colours</span></div>",
        body,
        "<div class=\"bt-palette-source\">", html_escape(source), "</div>",
        "</div>"
    )
}

# All palettes of one type
palette_cards <- function(type) {
    pals <- list_palettes(type)
    cards <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pals)), function(i) {
        palette_card(pals$name[i], pals$n[i], pals$source[i])
    }, "")
    knitr::asis_output(paste0("<div class=\"bt-palettes\">", paste(cards, collapse = "\n"), "</div>"))
}
```

bioToolkit has `r nrow(list_palettes())` palettes, taken from published
sources and credited below. Every plot has one `cols` argument that takes a
palette name, so this page is the menu: pick a palette by name, or pick
colours from it by their index.

| To | Use |
|---|---|
| colour a plot with a palette | `cols = "okabe-ito"` |
| reverse a palette | add `_r` to its name: `cols = "viridis_r"` |
| take some colours, in your order | `bt_palette("scanpy-20")[c(1, 3, 2)]` (indices as shown below) |
| get `n` colours | `bt_palette("seq-blue", n = 5)` (qualitative palettes give their first `n`) |
| see palettes, or your own colours, in R | `show_palettes()` |
| list names, types and sources | `list_palettes()` |
| check colours for colour blindness | `check_palette()` |

Hover a swatch to see its index and hex code. Qualitative palettes are for
groups (cell types, conditions); sequential palettes for values from low to
high (expression, significance); diverging palettes for values on both sides
of a centre (fold changes, z-scores, NES).

## Defaults

The plots use these palettes when `cols` is not given:

| Values | Default | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Groups, up to 20 | [`scanpy-20`](#palette-scanpy-20) | every plot coloured by group |
| Groups, 21 to 102 | [`scanpy-102`](#palette-scanpy-102) | every plot coloured by group |
| Expression on an embedding | [`plasma_r`](#palette-plasma) | `FeaturePlot_bioToolkit()` |
| Mean expression, not scaled | [`viridis_r`](#palette-viridis) | `DotPlot_bioToolkit()` |
| Mean expression, not scaled, heatmap | [`magma`](#palette-magma) | `DoHeatmap_bioToolkit()` |
| Significance, one-directional values | [`seq-purple`](#palette-seq-purple), [`seq-blue`](#palette-seq-blue), ... | enrichment plots (one hue per panel), `plot_pca()`, `plot_variance_explained()` |
| Signed values (z-scores, fold changes, NES) | [`blue-magenta`](#palette-blue-magenta) | dot plots, DE plots, enrichment NES, density differences, diverging feature plots |
| z-scores of single cells | [`teal-yellow`](#palette-teal-yellow) | `DoHeatmap_bioToolkit()` |

## Qualitative

For groups. They are never interpolated: a colour in between two group
colours would read as an intermediate group, so `bt_palette(name, n)` stops
when a palette has fewer than `n` colours.

```{r qualitative, echo = FALSE}
palette_cards("qualitative")
```

## Sequential

For values from low to high. The `seq-*` palettes are single-hue ramps
trimmed to the same lightness range (CIE L* 80 to 30): not so pale that low
values vanish on white, not so dark that the hue is lost, and the same value
has the same lightness whatever the hue, so that panels in different hues
stay comparable.

```{r sequential, echo = FALSE}
palette_cards("sequential")
```

## Diverging

For values on both sides of a centre, drawn in the middle colour. The plots
put the centre at 0 and stretch each side to its own end (see
[Colours](figures.html#colours)). Index 1 is the low end; for a scale of your
own, the low, middle and high colours are e.g.
`bt_palette("tol-burd")[c(1, 5, 9)]`.

```{r diverging, echo = FALSE}
palette_cards("diverging")
```

## Your own colours

`show_palettes()` draws palettes by name, a vector of your own colours, or a
list of both, with the index of each colour. For example, colours picked for
cell types next to the palette they came from:

```{r own-colours, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 1.6}
cell_cols <- bt_palette("scanpy-20")[c(1, 2, 3, 5, 4)]
names(cell_cols) <- c("CD4 T", "CD14 Mono", "B", "CD8 T", "NK")

show_palettes(list(
    "cell types" = cell_cols,
    "scanpy-20",
    warm = c("gold", "darkorange", "firebrick")
))
```

Name the colours by group and pass them as `cols`, so that each cell type
keeps its colour in every figure; `check_palette(cell_cols)` flags pairs that
become hard to tell apart with colour blindness (see
[Colour vision deficiency](figures.html#colour-vision-deficiency)).

## Adding a palette

New palettes come from a citable source, with hex values copied from it (or
from a package that reproduces it), never retyped from memory. Each is an
entry of `palette_list()` in `R/palettes.R`, with its colours, type and
source; the package tests check every entry.
